paper.title: Distribution oblivious, risk-aware algorithms for multi-armed bandits with unbounded rewards

settings.name_in_paper: Risk-aware, distribution oblivious fixed-budget best arm identification (mean + CVaR)
unmapped: Arm quality is the risk-aware metric xi_1*E[X(i)] + xi_2*CVaR_alpha(X(i)) (loss minimisation), not the mean
Learner knows the weights xi_1, xi_2 and the CVaR level alpha, but is distribution oblivious: does not know moment bound B, moment order p, or gaps
Arm distributions are continuous with strictly increasing CDF (condition C1)
Moment condition C2: E|X|^p < B for some p > 1 (not necessarily p <= 2)
settings.definition_quote: Consider a multi-armed bandit problem with $K$ arms ... The loss (or cost) associated with arm~$i$ is distributed as $X(i),$ where it is assumed that there exists $p > 1$ and $B < \infty$ such that $\Exp{|X(i)|^p} < B$ for all $i.$ ... Given a fixed budget of $T$ arm pulls in total, our goal is to identify the arm that minimizes $\xi_{1} \Exp{X(i)} + \xi_{2}\calp(X(i)),$ ... the algorithm does not have any prior information about the arm distributions, including the values of $p$ and $B.$

algorithms.name: Uniform exploration with truncated mean and truncated CVaR estimators (oblivious GSR special case)
Successive rejects with truncated mean and truncated CVaR estimators (oblivious)

bound.regime: T > K*n_star, n_star = max((12 xi_1 B/Delta[2])^(1/(q_m min(p-1,1))), (8 xi_2 B/(beta Delta[2]))^(1/(q_c (p-1))), (B/min(alpha,beta))^(1/(q_c p)), (Delta[2]/(8 xi_2))^(1/q_c))

symbols.Delta_min: Delta[2], smallest suboptimality gap in the metric xi_1 E[X] + xi_2 CVaR_alpha(X)
symbols.q_m: truncation exponent for mean estimator, b_m(n)=n^q_m
symbols.q_c: truncation exponent for CVaR estimator, b_c(n)=n^q_c, q_c in (0,1/2)
symbols.beta_c: 1 - alpha, where alpha is the CVaR confidence level
symbols.n_star: threshold defined in the theorem depending on B, p, alpha, Delta[2], xi_1, xi_2, q_m, q_c

conditions: arm distributions satisfy C1 (continuous, strictly increasing CDF)
arm distributions satisfy C2: E|X(i)|^p < B for some p > 1

source.label: ue-prob-of-error
source.quote: Suppose that the arm distributions satisfy the conditions C1 and C2. Under the uniform exploration algorithm, the probability of incorrect arm identification $p_e$ is bounded as $p_{e} \leq 2K\text{exp}\Big(-(T/K)^{1-q_m}\frac{\Delta[2]}{16\xi_{1}}\Big) + 6K \text{exp} \Big(-(T/K)^{1-2q_c} \frac{\beta \Delta[2]^{2}}{768 \xi_{2}^{2}}\Big)$ for $T> Kn^{*},$ where ...

results.notes: Paper's B, p, alpha, beta renamed implicitly inside n_star (beta_c = 1-alpha). Probability classified as 'expectation' since it bounds P(error).

bound.regime: T > K + K*logbar_K*n_star (n_star as in Theorem 3)

symbols.Delta_ord: Delta_ord(i) = Delta[i], i-th smallest suboptimality gap in metric xi_1 E[X] + xi_2 CVaR_alpha(X), 0<Delta[2]<=...<=Delta[K]
symbols.n_star: threshold defined in the theorem depending on B, p, alpha, Delta[2], xi_1, xi_2, q_m, q_c

conditions: arm distributions satisfy C1 (continuous, strictly increasing CDF)
arm distributions satisfy C2: E|X(i)|^p < B for some p > 1
tuning: n_k proportional to (T-K)/(K+1-k) as in Audibert-Bubeck successive rejects

source.label: sr-prob-of-error
source.quote: Let the arms satisfy the conditions C1 and C2. The probability of incorrect arm identification for the successive rejects algorithm is bounded as follows. p_e \leq \sum_{i=2}^{K} (K+1-i) 2\text{exp}(...) + \sum_{i=2}^{K} (K+1-i) 6\text{exp}(...) for $T> K+K\overline{\log}(K)n^{*}$

results.notes: Taking q_m=q, q_c=q/2 gives O(exp(-gamma T^{1-q})). Non-oblivious variant (exponential decay) is only sketched in Appendix D via lemmas, not recorded.
